results.content: Graph-based methods, pivotal for label inference over interconnected objects in many real-world applications, often encounter generalization challenges, if the graph used for model training differs significantly from the graph used for testing. The major challenge of developing PruneX is to learn models that well generalize to unseen circuits, i.e., the out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization problem. Our analysis further reveals how the decay rate of the $\tau$-mixing coefficient impacts the learning accuracy of the kernel ridge estimator with RFs. Extensive numerical experiments on both synthetic and real examples further validate our theoretical findings and support the effectiveness of the KRR with RFs in dealing with dependent data. We show several new use cases of IVON where we improve finetuning and model merging in Large Language Models, accurately predict generalization error, and faithfully estimate sensitivity to data. results.title: Foundation Models: Definition, Uses & Examples
results.content: While training a foundation model is expensive, **fine-tuning and inference are cost-efficient**, especially when amortized across many use cases or customers. For startups and enterprises aiming to build or fine-tune these models, understanding data sourcing, preparation, and governance is crucial. Startups may opt for **foundation model fine-tuning** or **adapter-based training** (LoRA, QLoRA, PEFT) to save time and cost. **Foundation models** are large-scale AI models trained on diverse, unlabeled data using self-supervised learning. What Are Foundation Models in Generative AI? #### What Are Foundation Models in Generative AI? In generative AI, foundation models serve as the underlying architecture that enables AI systems to create new content, text, images, audio, or code. LLMs like GPT-4 are considered **foundation models** because they’re trained on a broad range of text data and can be adapted to many tasks with minimal tuning. Foundation models provide the structure; generative AI is the output, like generating text, images, or code.
